alcoholic hyalin antigen is present in the sera of patients with alcoholic cirrhosis and alcoholic hepatitis, and that alcoholic hyalin antibody can be detected in the sera of alcoholic cirrhosis patients.

the sera of 30 patients with histologically confirmed alcoholic hepatitis are negative by SP-RIA and by immunofluorecence and complement fixation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of AHAg and anti-AH, which are considered to play an etiological role in the development of alcoholic hepatitis.

the detection of AHAg and anti-AH in alcoholic hepatitis by a solid-phase radioimmune assay (SP-RIA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alcoholic hyalin is not involved in the pathogenesis of alcoholic hepatitis.
AHAg and anti-AH were not found in sera of patients with alcoholic liver disease.
AH is not detectable in the serum of patients with histologically verified alcoholic hepatitis, and that AHAg and anti-AH are not useful diagnostic markers for alcoholic hepatitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alcoholic hyalin antigen is not detectable in the sera of patients with alcoholic liver disease.
alcoholic hyalin antigen and antibody are not detectable in patients with alcoholic hepatitis.
AH is not an auto-antigen in alcoholic hepatitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a sensitive solid phase radioimmunoassays (SP-RIA), which is a highly sensitive and specific method to detect alcoholic hyalin antigen in serum and anti-alcoholic hyalin antibody in sera of alcoholic liver disease.
the solid-phase radioimmunological method is a very sensitive technique for detection of alcoholic hepatitis-associated antigen and antibody.
the SP-RIA is a very sensitive method for the detection of AHAg and anti-AH in the sera of patients with alcoholic liver disease.
